action.description: The Action to perform when the client connection triggers the rule. Valid actions are "allow", "deny", "goto_next" and "apply_security_profile_group".
action.rationale: Determines whether traffic matching this rule is allowed, denied, passed to the next rule, or routed through a security profile group. This is the primary access-control decision the rule makes.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform is permitted to destroy this rule via IaC (DELETE/ABANDON/PREVENT). This is an infrastructure change-management control over the deployment tooling, not a property of the rule's live security configuration, so a platform-level security policy is not the right lever here.

description.description: An optional description for this resource.
description.rationale: Free-text metadata for human readability. It has no effect on how traffic is matched or enforced.

direction.description: The direction in which this rule applies. Possible values: ["INGRESS", "EGRESS"]
direction.rationale: Specifies whether the rule matches inbound (INGRESS) or outbound (EGRESS) traffic. It scopes the rule but neither value is inherently more or less secure than the other.

disabled.description:
Denotes whether the firewall policy rule is disabled.
When set to true, the firewall policy rule is not enforced and traffic behaves as if it did not exist.
If this is unspecified, the firewall policy rule will be enabled.
disabled.rationale: Controls whether the rule is enforced at all. When set to true, the rule is skipped entirely and traffic behaves as if it did not exist, silently removing whatever protection it provided.

enable_logging.description:
Denotes whether to enable logging for a particular rule.
If logging is enabled, logs will be exported to the configured export destination in Stackdriver.
Logs may be exported to BigQuery or Pub/Sub.
Note: you cannot enable logging on "goto_next" rules.
enable_logging.rationale: Controls whether traffic matching the rule is logged to Stackdriver. Disabling logging removes visibility needed for auditing and incident detection.

firewall_policy.description: The firewall policy of the resource.
firewall_policy.rationale: Identifies which parent firewall policy this rule belongs to. It is a reference/identifier, not a control over traffic.

priority.description:
An integer indicating the priority of a rule in the list.
The priority must be a positive value between 0 and 2147483647.
Rules are evaluated from highest to lowest priority where 0 is the highest priority and 2147483647 is the lowest prority.
priority.rationale: Sets the rule's evaluation order relative to other rules in the same policy. It has no single secure value; it only affects precedence, not what traffic is ultimately allowed or blocked.

security_profile_group.description:
A fully-qualified URL of a SecurityProfile resource instance.
Example: https://networksecurity.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{location}/securityProfileGroups/my-security-profile-group
Must be specified if action = 'apply_security_profile_group' and cannot be specified for other actions.
security_profile_group.rationale: References a specific SecurityProfile resource by its fully-qualified URL. We secure the referenced profile itself elsewhere; pinning or constraining this reference would require hardcoding a specific resource, which is overreaching.

target_resources.description:
A list of network resource URLs to which this rule applies.
This field allows you to control which network's VMs get this rule.
If this field is left blank, all VMs within the organization will receive the rule.
target_resources.rationale: A list of specific network resource URLs the rule applies to. This is a reference to team-specific resources rather than a security-configurable property of the rule itself.

target_service_accounts.description: A list of service accounts indicating the sets of instances that are applied with this rule.
target_service_accounts.rationale: Scopes the rule to instances by service-account identity — a selection/matching criterion, not a run-as execution identity. Constraining which specific service accounts a team may reference would require hardcoding team-specific values, which is overreaching.

tls_inspect.description:
Boolean flag indicating if the traffic should be TLS decrypted.
Can be set only if action = 'apply_security_profile_group' and cannot be set for other actions.
tls_inspect.rationale: Controls whether TLS traffic is decrypted for inspection when routed through a security profile group. Leaving it disabled hides encrypted traffic from threat inspection.

match.description: A match condition that incoming traffic is evaluated against. If it evaluates to true, the corresponding 'action' is enforced.

match.dest_address_groups.description: Address groups which should be matched against the traffic destination. Maximum number of destination address groups is 10.
match.dest_address_groups.rationale: References a managed address group by name. It points at a team-specific resource; we secure the referenced group itself, not this pointer.

match.dest_fqdns.description: Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) which should be matched against traffic destination. Maximum number of destination fqdn allowed is 100.
match.dest_fqdns.rationale: Domain names used purely as destination match criteria. This is a team-specific routing choice, not a generically enforceable security setting.

match.dest_ip_ranges.description: CIDR IP address range. Maximum number of destination CIDR IP ranges allowed is 5000.
match.dest_ip_ranges.rationale: CIDR ranges are team-specific network addressing. Segmentation and exposure are enforced by firewall/network-policy design, not by constraining the size or value of an address range here.

match.dest_network_context.description: Network context of the traffic destination. Possible values: ["UNSPECIFIED", "INTERNET", "INTRA_VPC", "NON_INTERNET", "VPC_NETWORKS"]
match.dest_network_context.rationale: Restricts destination matching by network context (e.g. internet vs intra-VPC). Setting this too broadly, such as INTERNET, when internal-only traffic was intended increases exposure.

match.dest_region_codes.description: Region codes whose IP addresses will be used to match for destination of traffic. Should be specified as 2 letter country code defined as per ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes. ex."US" Maximum number of dest region codes allowed is 5000.
match.dest_region_codes.rationale: Restricts destination matching by country. Relevant for geo-based access control and limiting exposure to unexpected regions.

match.dest_threat_intelligences.description: Names of Network Threat Intelligence lists. The IPs in these lists will be matched against traffic destination.
match.dest_threat_intelligences.rationale: Matches destination traffic against known-malicious-IP threat lists. This is a direct threat-blocking control.

match.src_address_groups.description: Address groups which should be matched against the traffic source. Maximum number of source address groups is 10.
match.src_address_groups.rationale: References a managed address group by name, pointing at a team-specific resource rather than a configurable security property of this rule.

match.src_fqdns.description: Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) which should be matched against traffic source. Maximum number of source fqdn allowed is 100.
match.src_fqdns.rationale: Domain names used purely as source match criteria — a team-specific routing choice, not a generic security configuration.

match.src_ip_ranges.description: CIDR IP address range. Maximum number of source CIDR IP ranges allowed is 5000.
match.src_ip_ranges.rationale: CIDR ranges are team-specific network addressing; segmentation is enforced by firewall/network-policy design, not by constraining this value directly.

match.src_network_context.description: Network context of the traffic source. Possible values: ["UNSPECIFIED", "INTERNET", "INTRA_VPC", "NON_INTERNET", "VPC_NETWORKS"]
match.src_network_context.rationale: Restricts source matching by network context. Setting this too broadly increases the pool of traffic the rule applies to.

match.src_networks.description: Networks of the traffic source. It can be either a full or partial url.
match.src_networks.rationale: VPC network URLs referencing specific networks. This is a resource reference, not a security-configurable property we can generically constrain.

match.src_region_codes.description: Region codes whose IP addresses will be used to match for source of traffic. Should be specified as 2 letter country code defined as per ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes. ex."US" Maximum number of source region codes allowed is 5000.
match.src_region_codes.rationale: Restricts source matching by country. Relevant to geo-fencing and mitigating traffic from unexpected regions.

match.src_threat_intelligences.description: Names of Network Threat Intelligence lists. The IPs in these lists will be matched against traffic source.
match.src_threat_intelligences.rationale: Matches source traffic against known-malicious-IP threat lists. This is a direct threat-blocking control.

match.layer4_configs.description: Pairs of IP protocols and ports that the rule should match.

match.layer4_configs.ip_protocol.description:
The IP protocol to which this rule applies. The protocol type is required when creating a firewall rule.
This value can either be one of the following well known protocol strings (tcp, udp, icmp, esp, ah, ipip, sctp), or the IP protocol number.
match.layer4_configs.ip_protocol.rationale: Selects which IP protocol the rule matches. This is a functional/architectural choice with no universally secure value — a legitimate rule may need to match any protocol depending on the workload.

match.layer4_configs.ports.description:
An optional list of ports to which this rule applies. This field is only applicable for UDP or TCP protocol. Each entry must be either an integer or a range. If not specified, this rule applies to connections through any port.
Example inputs include: ["22"], ["80","443"], and ["12345-12349"].
match.layer4_configs.ports.rationale: Selects which ports the rule matches. Port selection depends entirely on the workload's application requirements; there is no single compliant value a generic platform policy can enforce.

match.src_secure_tags.description: List of secure tag values, which should be matched at the source of the traffic. For INGRESS rule, if all the srcSecureTag are INEFFECTIVE, and there is no srcIpRange, this rule will be ignored. Maximum number of source tag values allowed is 256.

match.src_secure_tags.name.description: Name of the secure tag, created with TagManager's TagValue API.
match.src_secure_tags.name.rationale: References a specific secure tag value by name. We secure the referenced tag itself, not this pointer to it.

target_secure_tags.description:
A list of secure tags that controls which instances the firewall rule applies to.
If targetSecureTag are specified, then the firewall rule applies only to instances in the VPC network that have one of those EFFECTIVE secure tags, if all the targetSecureTag are in INEFFECTIVE state, then this rule will be ignored.
targetSecureTag may not be set at the same time as targetServiceAccounts. If neither targetServiceAccounts nor targetSecureTag are specified, the firewall rule applies to all instances on the specified network. Maximum number of target secure tags allowed is 256.

target_secure_tags.name.description: Name of the secure tag, created with TagManager's TagValue API.
target_secure_tags.name.rationale: References a specific secure tag value by name used to scope which instances the rule applies to — a reference, not a generically constrainable security property.
